title: Introduce credential surge controller + compact cross-sdk stream facade for ergonomic retries
author: Nina Chung
description: Motivation: We repeatedly see short bursty spikes of reauths and token refreshes from multi-tenant SDK usage (especially under autoscale and rapid reconnect patterns). This PR introduces a small, cross-language control plane (Credential Surge Controller) plus a compact stream facade in Python/TypeScript/Go to reduce reauth storms, standardize retry presets, and improve ergonomics for async streaming consumers. High-level changes: 1) Credential Surge Controller: central prefetch + rate-limited refresh queue that coalesces overlapping reauth attempts and exposes lightweight telemetry hooks; it runs per-process and can be configured via SDK config (prefetch_window, max_concurrent_refresh, jitter_strategy). 2) Compact Stream Facade: ergonomic async iterator / async generator wrappers (py: CompactPullStream, ts: compactAsyncGenerator, go: CompactStreamIterator) that integrate with the controller and the existing retry profiles; they surface a small set of lifecycle hooks (onConsume, onPause, onResume, onBackoff) to make client cancellation, checkpointing and backpressure easier. 3) Retry ergonomics: new retry presets (surge-aware, low-latency, bulk-batch) and clearer default timeouts to avoid cascading fails while preserving low tail latency. 4) Cross-SDK parity: aligned surface and docs for the three SDKs and bumped package versions (python 1.9.0, typescript 1.28.0, go 1.5.3). 5) Tests & telemetry: unit tests for controller logic, integration smoke tests exercising burst reconnect patterns, and a README section with recommended configs for Dedicated/Docker deployments. Checklist: [x] implement controller core and queueing; [x] add facade wrappers in py/ts/go; [x] add retry presets and config knobs; [x] documentation and changelog entries; [x] automated tests and CI passing; [x] version bumps and release notes. Backwards compatibility: the controller is opt-in via a top-level SDK config flag (credential_surge_controller.enabled=false by default) to avoid behavioral changes in existing customers. When enabled, some internal retry timing changes apply (described in release notes). See linked SUP ticket for a customer-reported incident that motivated this change.
